description: Dialogue for the Thieves Guild fence who gives and receives debt collection quests

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Keep your voice down. What do you want?

choices.text: I completed the job - Brennan's debt.
The rival crew will not be a problem.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Work? You think we hand out jobs to anyone who walks up? You need to prove yourself first. Talk to the recruiter if you haven't already. After you're in, then we talk business.

choices.text: Where do I find the recruiter?

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Ah, yes. The ledger job. Clean work. You've got potential. We have a... delicate matter that needs handling. A sailor named Brennan owes the Guild a considerable sum. 150 gold. He's been drinking it away at the Rusty Anchor instead of paying his debts.

choices.text: What do you want me to do?

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Find him, get the gold, bring it here. I do not need to hear how. What I need is no guards, and no story going round the harbour.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Good. Brennan spends most evenings at the Rusty Anchor. He's the one with the nervous look and empty coin purse. Get the gold and come straight back here. And remember - no guards.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Brennan borrowed 150 gold three weeks ago. Said he needed it for 'ship repairs.' Instead, he's been buying rounds for the whole tavern. The Guild doesn't like being made a fool of. Find him at the Rusty Anchor and collect. Will you do it?

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Your loss. Come back if you change your mind.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Ah, you're back. Did you get the gold from Brennan?

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Excellent work. The Guild appreciates your... efficiency. Here's your cut - 50 gold. And this reputation boost will serve you well. Keep proving yourself and more lucrative opportunities will come your way.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: The recruiter operates in the shadows. Look for a hooded figure in the market district after dark. They'll approach you if you seem... promising.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: We take work. We do not take from our own, and we do not bring the watch to this door. That is the whole of it, and it is more than I usually tell anyone standing where you are.

nodes.speaker: Fence
nodes.text: Stay out of trouble. Or at least, don't get caught.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: Handled is a word with a lot of room in it. Narrow it down for me, because I have to decide what I tell the guild, and I would rather decide it now than in front of them.

choices.text: I paid him. He is leaving the city.
I put the fear in him. He will never talk again.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: Then nobody hears anything from Tomas again, and nobody hears anything from the six people he was about to name either, and that is worth more to us than it should be. Clean, permanent, and expensive in ways you will notice later. Your cut.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: Bought. Fine - a man who takes money to leave will take money to come back, but by then he is out of the city and out of anyone's reach, and the guild has not had to bury anybody. Your cut. Do not tell me what it cost you.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: Frightened. That works right up until somebody frightens him harder, and the watch is very good at frightening people harder. Still - he is silent today, and today is what I was asked about. Your cut.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: You let him walk. ... I am going to write down that he could not be found, and you are going to remember that I did that for you, and one day I am going to remind you. Take your cut, and take a long look at the door on your way out.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: The rival crew. Tell me what is left of them.

choices.text: A line down the middle of the district. They keep the docks.
It went badly. They are still there, and now they know my face.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: Broken. Every corner of that district is ours and every thief in it is frightened of us, which is efficient and is also how you end up with three new crews in a year, because frightened men organise. Your cut. Enjoy the quiet while it lasts.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: A line. Old-fashioned. Everybody keeps breathing and everybody knows where they stand, and in two years somebody young decides the line is an insult. That is two years from now. Your cut.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: You brought them in. Eleven experienced thieves who spent last winter robbing us, now sitting in our rooms hearing our business. That is either the best week this guild has had in a decade, or the beginning of something I will be blamed for. Your cut, and a great deal of my attention from now on.

nodes.speaker: Guild Fence
nodes.text: So they are still there, they are angry, and they can pick you out of a crowd. I have seen worse outcomes. Not many. Take your cut - it is a small one, and you know why.
